Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

I am sending this version to station manager Priya Nair for review. Priya, please check the three open items in the numbered section and tell me which option to enter for each one. The rest of the schedule is shown as planned, not as a list of decisions still waiting to be made. The main studio is in the North Quay building, and the small production room is available when no recording is booked there.

The weekday morning schedule starts with the local bulletin at 6:30, followed by First Light with Inez Park from 7:00 to 9:00. Inez has confirmed the time, and she will take the news handover from the bulletin reader at seven. The 9:00 slot is Open Table, a call-in program hosted by Lewis Grant, and the current plan is for Lewis to use the production room for the first half hour while the main studio is reset. At 10:00, the music desk takes over with a recorded set prepared by volunteers. The noon bulletin stays at noon; it is not being moved to make room for a longer interview. On Tuesday, the local council segment is scheduled inside Open Table, from 9:20 to 9:35, and Lewis has agreed to take the questions in that segment.

The afternoon pattern is the same on all five weekdays unless a program is listed separately. At 1:00, Field Notes is hosted by Aria Bell, who records short reports about gardens, waterways, and public transport. Her Friday edition will be live, since she has booked the main studio for that hour. The regular 2:00 music program, Small Frequencies, is presented by Niko James and uses the station’s locally made music library. Niko has asked Mara to keep the last ten minutes open on Wednesday for a short conversation with a visiting record-shop owner; Mara has placed a hold there, but the guest has not confirmed. At 3:00, the schedule returns to the volunteer music desk. The 4:30 bulletin is read by whoever is listed on the daily staffing sheet, rather than by a single regular presenter.

After the evening bulletin, the schedule includes a mix of live and recorded programs. On Monday, Sound Map runs from 6:00 to 7:00, with recordings supplied by the station’s neighborhood contributors. The Tuesday 6:00 slot is still marked for a repeat of the Saturday arts interview, because the original file is already cleared for another broadcast. On Wednesday, the youth program Back Steps is live from 6:00 to 6:45, and host Samira Cole has asked to keep the phone line open for listener questions. I have left the next fifteen minutes unassigned rather than extending the show without her agreement. Thursday’s 6:00 program is a recorded conversation about the history of the ferry terminal. On Friday, the 7:00 slot is reserved for the monthly volunteer meeting broadcast, with the meeting expected to finish by 8:00; the overnight music sequence begins at 8:00 as usual.

Tom Arlen, the station engineer, checked the transmitter log on May 27 and reported that the normal signal test was completed. He also told me, “The cooling fan is louder than last month, but the readings stayed within the usual range.” Tom has not asked for a schedule change, and his note does not say that the fan has failed. He proposed a maintenance visit for Thursday, June 5, between 5:30 and 6:30 p.m., when the building is usually quiet. The visit is not yet in the engineering diary because the building caretaker has not confirmed access. I have kept the Thursday ferry-terminal program in its normal 6:00 slot for now. If the visit runs past 6:30, Tom says the station should use the backup studio for the bulletin and delay the recorded program until 6:45; if it finishes on time, the listed schedule stays in place. Please do not enter either change unless the visit is confirmed and the timing condition applies.

1. On Wednesday, Niko’s requested conversation is only a hold, not a confirmed guest booking. Should I leave the final ten minutes of Small Frequencies open, or restore the regular music selection if the guest has not confirmed by Tuesday at noon? Niko asked Mara for the hold, and Mara is asking Priya which schedule treatment to use. I have not told Niko that either option has been approved.
2. For Saturday, Daniel Cho has proposed a one-hour archive feature at 10:00 a.m. in place of the usual volunteer music desk. Daniel has a set of recordings from the station’s first year, but he has not delivered the edited program. Should I reserve the slot provisionally until Friday, or keep the regular desk in the grid? Daniel proposed the feature to Mara; this is not yet a request from the volunteer desk to give up its slot.
3. The Sunday 4:00 community noticeboard currently has two possible readers, Jo Price and Malik Ford. Jo told me she can read it if she is back from the market by 3:30, while Malik has said he is available for the whole afternoon. Please tell me whether to list Malik as the confirmed reader and Jo as the alternate, or to leave both names pending until Sunday morning. I have not asked either person to swap with the other.

The Saturday schedule otherwise starts with the 8:00 local bulletin, followed by the volunteer music desk from 8:30 to 10:00.
